title: NRG Security Baseline (CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations v7.0.0)
status: v2.0 (2026-10-25, owner's decision): the baseline follows the CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 and nothing else. Minimum is the E3 Level 1 profile, Standard adds the E5-only Level 1 recommendations, Hardened adds Level 2. A recommendation an assessment control checks is that control's row; one no control checks, or checks only in part, is a manual CIS-<number> row that always resolves NotVerified. v1.x NRG-only requirements (VM-VERIFY-01 and every control with no CIS citation) are assessment-only now: still assessed and reported, never required.
purpose: The CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations v7.0.0 recommendations NRG requires of every managed client, by tier. A desired-state layer over the assessment: it reads findings and never changes them, creates none, and moves no framework score. A control absent from this file is assessment-only.
note: Governance only. Nothing tenant-specific lives here: licensing comes from the tenant SKUs (license gating), the EDR from clients.json or -ThirdPartyEDR, skipped collectors from the assessment scope, and approved deviations from Config/baseline-exceptions/<tenant-domain>.psd1.

tiers.Minimum: CIS E3 Level 1: every applicable managed environment; a deviation needs a written explanation.
tiers.Standard: CIS E5 Level 1: Minimum plus the recommendations CIS lists for E5 only.
tiers.Hardened: CIS Level 2: Minimum and Standard plus every Level 2 recommendation, for elevated-risk or regulated environments.

slaClasses.Immediate: Actively exploited; the day counts live in the operations policy, not here.

freshnessNote: Evidence older than its class window is not evidence: the control resolves NotVerified. Windows carry one day of slack over the nominal cadence so a run that starts a few hours late does not flip every control.
effectivenessNote: Configuration compliance and effectiveness are different questions. EffectivenessCapability says whether the assessment can read the effectiveness evidence today; where it cannot, EffectivenessState is Unknown and is reported as Unknown, never rounded to a pass.

controls.Title: Break-Glass Accounts Configured
controls.EvidenceSource: Graph: PIM role policies, consent settings, app-registration settings (Invoke-TPCollectAADIdentityGovernance)
controls.ExpectedState: CIS 1.1.2: Ensure two emergency access accounts have been defined. Checked as: At least two cloud-only accounts permanently assigned Global Administrator are kept as emergency access accounts, excluded from every Conditional Access policy that would otherwise reach them. While Security Defaults is enabled (it cannot exclude any account), they are confirmed to exist, with credentials held offline and an MFA method registered for each. This control checks part of the recommendation; the rest is a separate manual row.
controls.EffectivenessCheck: A quarterly test sign-in from each account succeeds and is logged (AAD-10.3, manual today).
controls.Reason: Without a documented break-glass pair, a CA misconfiguration or MFA outage locks NRG out of the tenant it manages.
controls.WhyMspOwnsThis: CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations v7.0.0 1.1.2 (E3 Level 1 / E5 Level 1), the profile this tier adopts.
controls.Notes: Excluded from CA, monitored on sign-in (AAD-10.3 is the manual twin), FIDO2 or long random passwords in the vault. Two or more accounts need a human check that they are the right ones. Partially automated: the tool proves fewer than two break-glass accounts; two or more still needs a human to confirm they are the right accounts.
